steps.title: Find an issue to work on
steps.summary: Pick a task from the issue templates, favouring issues labelled `good first issue` or `help wanted`. Naming the component in the title (`[receiver/foo] …`) or in the template's Component(s) field makes a workflow apply that component's label and ping its code owners as soon as the issue is filed.

steps.title: Understand how issues are triaged
steps.summary: Read the triage process, the label definitions and the state diagram so you know what `needs triage`, `waiting-for-codeowners` and `help wanted` mean before you volunteer for the work.

steps.title: Read the contributing guide
steps.summary: CONTRIBUTING.md covers building and running the collector locally, linting and tests, changelog rules, PR titles, labels via comments, roles and the Makefile guidelines. Start here before writing any code.

steps.title: Scaffold the component and its metadata
steps.summary: For a new component, create the directory with a metadata.yaml declaring type, class, stability and codeowners, a doc.go with the mdatagen generate pragma, and a README status stub — then run the generators that fill in the boilerplate.

steps.title: Add tests
steps.summary: Every change should ship with tests that actually validate it. Keep long-running suites behind the `integration` or `e2e` build tags so the default test run stays fast and credential-free.

steps.title: Lint and run the test suite
steps.summary: Run the repo-level lint and test targets before opening the pull request. They wrap the module-level targets across every Go module, so one command covers the whole repository.

steps.title: Add a changelog entry
steps.summary: User-facing changes need a YAML entry in .chloggen. Create it from your branch name, fill in every field, then validate it — user-visible changes go to CHANGELOG.md and API changes to CHANGELOG-API.md.

steps.title: Open the pull request
steps.summary: Fill in every section of the PR template — description, link to tracking issue, testing, documentation and the authorship attestation — and title it `[component/type] short statement` so reviewers know at a glance what changed.

steps.title: Get code owner review and merge
steps.summary: CODEOWNERS maps each path to its maintainers, so reviewers are requested automatically and a facilitator is assigned. Address their comments; once an approver approves, the `ready to merge` label tells a maintainer the PR can land — and ownership changes need `make update-codeowners` first.
